texts.preamble: Registrar Of Companies vs M/S. Gayatri Remedies Limited on 24 December, 2020
texts.facts: The State preferred criminal appeal in the Court of Session under Section 378 (1) (a) of the Cr.P.C. The objection qua the maintainability of the said appeal in view of Section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C. was rejected by the Court of Session. 8. In the said case, the appellant preferred a petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
texts.arguments: 3. Ld. Counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is entitled to prefer an appeal against a judgment of acquittal in view of amended section 372 of the Cr.P.C. He submitted that after the Amendment Act 5 of 2009, a right of appeal to the victims has been incorporated and definition of 'victim' has been introduced in the Cr.P.C. He submitted that appellant being the victim is entitled to prefer an appeal against the order of acquittal in a case under section 99 and 137 (3) of the Act. 4. Ld. Counsel for the respondent No. 2 to submitted that right of appeal provided to the victim in amended section 372 of the Cr.P.C. is not meant for the complainant of a case under section 99 and 137 (3) of the Act. submitted that appropriate remedy to the appellant is to seek special leave to appeal from the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi under section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C. He relied on judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Subhash Chand vs. State, (2013) 2 SCC 17. He submitted that the present appeal is not maintainable. In 'The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. vs. Prabhu Dayal' Crl. A. 972/2012 decided on 03.09.2014, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court considered remedy available in the case of acquittal in a case instituted on a complaint case, held as under" "18. 7. In Subhash Chand's (supra) case, the respondent instituted a complaint case against the appellant alleging therein that he violated certain provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1994. The matter reached to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India examined the issue whether in a complaint case, an appeal from an order of acquittal of the Magistrate would lie to the Sessions Court under Section 378 (1) (a) of the Cr.P.C. or to the High Court under Section 378 (4) of the Cr.P.C. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court and the complainant cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court, as under: Registrar Of Companies vs M/S. Gayatri Remedies Limited on 24 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131250406/ 2 "21.
